analysis: Changes: (1) docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md line 3 date bump and new line 119 row describing provider-staged (non-native-bound) checkpoint import: destinations built from zeroed host bytes, skipping eval/stream fences so staging never waits on MLX evalLock; zero source may briefly commit up to one destination outside the MLX allocator and the import plan charges the largest as staging scratch. (2) libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer bump 14661d9->c17693f; the submodule source (CheckpointHostZeros.swift, PagedCheckpointStorage.swift, CompleteCheckpointImportPlan.swift, etc.) is NOT supplied, so the behavior change implied by the doc row cannot be verified. (3) New opt-in live test ModelCheckpointRestoreContentionLiveTests.swift (gated by DARKBLOOM_RESTORE_CONTENTION_BENCHMARK=1 and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_EXCLUSIVE_GPU=1) measuring SSD restore TTFT vs cold under idle/foreign-prefill/post-donor conditions; uses distinct per-condition tenant scopes and writes a timing report to a new absolute path. It is test-only, introduces no production attack surface, and does not widen cache scope, TTL, key handling or on-disk metadata. Relevant threats: T-041 (cross-tenant TTFT oracle, SEC-035; test code only measures its own scopes), T-028/TB-007 (residual host/GPU memory), T-010/T-029 (availability). Unverified contract for next pass: the submodule change that skips eval/stream fences and uses host zeros must preserve fully-initialized destinations, correct scratch accounting against GlobalKVCacheBudget, and not leak prior-request data (reading zeros means no stale data exposure if implemented as described); reviewers with the submodule diff should confirm. No identity-binding, encryption, TTL or on-disk format changes are in the supplied evidence. needs_deeper_review is set because the submodule diff is not visible.
